name: Unity infinite loop crash
goal: While optimizing code, Unity crashed. The crash information did not look very familiar, because it never happened before. Because I optimized the code in steps, saving and testing after each step, it was easier to figure out the issue.

approach.text: First, I verified that the crash was caused by the code, not on accident, so I ran the game again, and it crashed again as expected. The crash report was not very clear for me.<<image 6.png>>I recognized the MemoryManager and remembered the terms "allocating memory", which led me to believe the issue was in an overflow of memory. From previous projects, I knew this was most of the times caused by an infinite loop, or an unintentional recursive function. In the updated code, I destroyed the gameobject in the OnDestroy function of a script attached to that gameobject. After making the function not a Unity function by renaming it, the crash no longer occurred.

normalLearnings: I learned that Destroy does not just destroy the gameobject, it calls the OnDestroy function of every script, if it has one.
I learned what a stack overflow exception looks like in Unity.
validation: Since renaming the method was the only difference I made, I am certain that this was the cause of the issue.
contribution: The crash was cause while optimizing code, which directly contributes to the solution.
